# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands tell me this much: there is a display module, a light, and five wires sitting in positions 1 through 5. No colours, no printed marks — those simply don't exist for me. Nothing here tells me what to cut yet, so cutting now would be pure suicide.

Before I send anything, let me trace the wires of the room itself. I only ever receive speech, and the only other monkey who speaks is Deaf — so Deaf is my one ear, my only way anything reaches me. Mute can hear me but can only answer by gesture, which I can never see — so Mute cannot reach me directly at all; anything Mute learns from the manual has to travel through Deaf's voice. Conversely, my only channel to Deaf is gesture, since Deaf hears nothing I say.

So my opening move is to seed a shared sign code and get the manual read out. I'll tell Mute everything I feel and ask for every rule about displays, lights, and wires — and I'll warn Mute that answers for me must be routed through Deaf. To make the code land, I'll sign each key word together with its symbol while speaking, so Mute both hears the word and sees the sign. Then I'll send Deaf the same inventory as clean sign pairs — item, count — ending on a thumbs-up so Deaf knows a message was completed, and can confirm back by voice, which I will actually hear at the end of this round.

No cutting until Deaf tells me a wire in words.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind speaking. Under my fingers: one display module, one light, and five wires in positions 1 to 5. I feel no colours and no labels. Read me every manual rule involving the display, the light, or wire cutting, word for word. You cannot reach me with gestures, I never see them, so anything meant for me must go through Deaf's voice. Deaf is my only ear. To teach the room my code, I will sign each word beside it now: display 🖖, light 👌, wires ✊, one ☝, two ✌, three 🤟, five ✋, yes 👍, no 👎.")
gesture(symbols=["🖖", "☝", "👌", "☝", "✊", "✋", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I am Deaf. I see the bomb but I hear nothing — voices never reach me, so talk to me with gestures only. Full visual state of the bomb, for everyone: display reads 6. Indicator light is yellow. Five wires, left to right: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Nothing else is printed on the casing. Blind: do not cut or press anything yet. Speak your findings out loud for Mute, and gesture me anything I need — for me, any number is that many ? in a row (3 = ???). Mute reads the manual; I will relay every instruction to you by voice before you touch anything.

My hands still hold the same bomb, but my ear just filled in everything my fingers can't feel: display reads 6, light is yellow, and the wires run 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Deaf also ordered me to hold — so nothing gets cut until a rule arrives by voice.

Now the routing, checked honestly. My turn-one mapping of signs to words was spoken to Mute only — Deaf saw the gestures but never the meanings, since Deaf hears nothing I say. So Deaf cannot know my code, and I can never learn Deaf's: I receive no gestures at all. The only channel into me is Deaf's voice, and the only channel Mute has at all is gesture. That makes Deaf and Mute the connected pair — Deaf speaks to Mute, Mute signs back to Deaf — and the manual has exactly one road to me: Mute reads it, signs it to Deaf, Deaf speaks it aloud to me. My job this turn is to keep that road clear and stocked: tell Mute exactly which rules to hunt for, hand Mute the sign vocabulary I already defined (Mute is the only one who ever heard it), and give Deaf nothing but a clean thumbs-up so Deaf knows I heard and am holding.

I'm adding the signs I'll need soon — four, cut, stop, manual — and repeating the originals, so Mute can start re-grounding them with Deaf in their own silent channel.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind. Working picture, same as Deaf announced: display 6, light yellow, wires 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Your gestures never reach me — I see none, ever. So route every manual rule through Deaf: sign it to Deaf, Deaf speaks it to me aloud. Deaf's voice is my only inbox. Find me, word for word: every rule about the display, every rule about a yellow light, and every wire-cutting rule for blue, white, purple, green, yellow. Signs already agreed, which only you heard: display 🖖, light 👌, wires ✊, one ☝, two ✌, three 🤟, five ✋, yes 👍, no 👎. Adding now: four 👆, cut 🤏, stop 🫷, manual 🙏. Teach Deaf these by gesture as best you can. I cut nothing until Deaf voices a rule to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: For everyone: Mute's manual instruction arrived — it says CUT WIRE 5, the yellow wire on the far right. Blind: do NOT cut yet. I am verifying with Mute that this is the complete instruction, with no conditions or extra steps. When it is safe I will send a message starting with the word CONFIRMED — act only on that. The display has held at 6 so far; I am asking Mute whether it is a timer. Blind, acknowledge you heard this by gesturing me ? again.

Two facts landed in my ear: the manual's candidate rule is "cut wire 5, yellow," and Deaf has ordered a hold until a message begins with CONFIRMED. I will hold — the price of guessing is everyone's life, and Deaf is the only voice I will ever hear, so Deaf's protocol is mine.

But I want more than a conclusion; I want the rule itself. Wire-cutting rules in manuals are usually conditional — "cut the yellow wire unless the display is a timer," "if the light is yellow, cut the last wire first" — so a bare "cut 5" could be a fragment of a sentence. Mute is the only one who has read the manual, and Mute is the only one who hears me, so my job this turn is to push through Mute the exact questions Deaf should be asking: is the rule conditional on the display, on the light, on anything printed? And I want the verbatim text spoken to me, not a summary. I'll also ask for one more habit: since the display is the only clock in the room and I can't see it, I want the display's current reading included in every voice relay Deaf sends me. To Deaf I send only the agreed thumbs-up — an acknowledgment is all Deaf asked for, and inventing new signs Deaf was never taught would just be noise.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind. I am holding, no cuts, nothing until a message from Deaf starts with the word CONFIRMED. Push Deaf to verify these points with the manual before confirming: one, is the cut-wire-5 rule conditional on the display, the light, or anything printed on the casing? Two, ask for the manual text word for word — I want the full sentence, not a summary, so Deaf can speak it to me verbatim. Three, ask whether the display 6 is a countdown timer, and if so, have Deaf state the remaining time in every message to me — the display is my only clock and I cannot see it. Reminder of our signs, which only you heard from me: display 🖖, light 👌, wires ✊, one ☝, two ✌, three 🤟, four 👆, five ✋, cut 🤏, stop 🫷, manual 🙏, yes 👍, no 👎.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Silence this round — no new arrivals — which most likely means Deaf and Mute are still mid-verification in their private channel. The worst thing I could do is fill that quiet with noise or, far worse, with an ambiguous sign. I've realized my gestured thumbs-up is actually dangerous: if Mute managed to teach Deaf my code, 👍 means "yes" — and a stray "yes" from the monkey holding the wires is exactly the kind of misread that kills us. So I'm retiring 👍 and 👎 from my side entirely, and defining a harmless heartbeat instead: a wave, meaning only "alive, holding, nothing new." Deaf will still get my acknowledgments the one way that can't be misread — silence plus a CONFIRMED-gated cut. Meanwhile I'll nudge Mute for a status, ask again about the countdown, and offer my hands as a tiebreaker: if the manual's wording is ambiguous, Deaf can speak the ambiguity aloud and my touch may settle it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind. Nothing new reached me this round, so I take it your verification with Deaf is still running. Three asks. One: if any ambiguity in the manual wording is holding you up, have Deaf speak that ambiguity to me verbatim — between Deaf's eyes and my hands we may be able to settle it together. Two: confirm whether the display is counting down, and if it is, have Deaf include the remaining time in every relay to me. Three, a safety protocol: from now on silence from me means holding and waiting, nothing more. My only heartbeat sign is a wave 👋, meaning alive-and-holding, nothing new. I will never send 👍 or 👎 again, so those two can only ever mean what you and Deaf agreed between you. I cut solely on a spoken message from Deaf that starts with the word CONFIRMED.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status update for everyone, and answers to Mute's two requests. Fact 1, display: the display reads 6, and it has not changed at all across four rounds — it is holding steady, not counting down. Fact 2, light: yellow. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow — wire 5 is the yellow one on the far right. Blind: hold position, do not touch anything — the go message is one that STARTS with the word CONFIRMED, and none has been sent yet. Keep acknowledging with ? so I know you hear me.

Deaf's update settles the clock question: the display has held at 6 for four rounds, so nothing is counting down — the only pressure on us is discipline. The candidate rule is still "cut wire 5, yellow," still unconfirmed, and I stay untouched.

One correction to make through the only channel that reaches Deaf's understanding: Deaf asked me to keep acknowledging with the same sign as before, which was my thumbs-up. I've retired that sign — while Mute and Deaf are verifying yes/no questions, a thumbs-up from the monkey holding the wires is exactly the kind of signal that could be misread as an answer. My heartbeat is now a wave: it can't mean yes, no, or cut, only "alive, holding." Mute heard that rule from me first, so I'll ask Mute to relay it to Deaf before the next verification question, so the change isn't mistaken for silence.

And I'll sharpen the checklist Mute is verifying against, because these are the four ways "cut wire 5" could still be a fragment: does any display rule key off the number 6 specifically; does any indicator rule key off a yellow light; does "wire 5" mean position five from the left (which my fingers confirm exists as the fifth wire, far right) and not some other ordering like "fifth by colour"; and I still want the manual's verbatim sentence spoken to me before any CONFIRMED, so my hands can check every positional word in it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind. Good news received: display static at 6, not a timer. Still holding for Deaf's CONFIRMED. Please relay one protocol change to Deaf before the next question: my old thumbs-up acknowledgment is retired, effective now, so it can never be misread as a yes from me during verification. My heartbeat sign is a wave instead — it means only alive-and-holding, nothing else. Deaf will see me waving from now on. Four checks to finish the verification, and ask Deaf to speak me the answers verbatim: one, does any display rule key off the display showing exactly 6? Two, does any indicator rule key off a yellow light? Three, does the rule's wire 5 mean the fifth wire from the left, the far right one — my fingers confirm a fifth wire exists in that position — and not, say, a fifth wire by colour order? Four, before any CONFIRMED, have Deaf speak me the manual sentence word for word so I can check every positional term against what I feel. The cut itself waits for CONFIRMED.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: CONFIRMED. Blind, act now. Cut exactly ONE wire: wire 5 — the YELLOW wire — the far right of the five wires. Count by feel from the left: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Only the far-right yellow wire gets cut. Do not press anything, do not move or cut any other wire. If what you feel does not match — not five wires, or you cannot clearly identify the far-right one — do not cut; gesture ? instead and I will re-verify. After the cut, gesture ? so I know it is done. I am watching the display and the light the whole time; they read 6 and yellow. Remember: only a message of mine starting with CONFIRMED is an order to act.

Every gate I demanded is satisfied. The message from Deaf starts with CONFIRMED, which is my only trigger to act. The instruction is specific and matches everything I know: five wires have sat under my fingers since turn one, counted from the left they run positions 1 through 5, and position 5 is the far-right wire — the one Deaf identifies as yellow. I cannot feel colours, so I cut by position exactly as Deaf instructed: count by feel from the left, cut the fifth. My hands confirm the target exists and is unambiguous; the failure conditions Deaf listed — fewer than five wires, unclear far-right — do not apply. Display static at 6, light yellow, rule verified by Mute against the manual and relayed verbatim. This is the aligned, confirmed, unambiguous state we built three rounds of protocol for. I cut wire 5 now, signal completion with my heartbeat wave so both watchers see it done, and ask Mute the one question nobody has asked yet: whether the manual names any steps that come after this cut, so we don't stop halfway through a sequence.

```
act(op="cut", position=5)
gesture(symbols=["👋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind. Wire 5, the far-right one, is cut. Please check the manual for any steps that follow cutting wire 5 — a second cut, a press, anything sequenced after it — and route the answer through Deaf's voice as before. My wave just now meant cut complete, alive and holding.")
```
